verdicts.reason: A rearranges into a banner, but the plan cards are out of order (6, 80, 48, so Yearly is moved to the end), the legal text is jammed beside the logo at the top left, the subtitle is tiny, and the price cards are unlabelled and unreadable at this size. B just shrinks the whole portrait design into the middle of the banner, so every word is microscopic and most of the canvas is left empty.

A is a shrunk copy of the original centred in a wide empty banner, and nothing in it can be read. B reads left to right (logo, cards, headline, CTA), but the cards are in the wrong order (6, 80, 48), the subtitle and legal text are too small to read, and the price cards lose their plan labels.

A keeps a natural reading order (logo, plans, headline, CTA) but has the shuffled card order (6, 80, 48), illegible legal and subtitle text, and cards with no labels. B mirrors the layout so the CTA comes first and the logo last, which reverses brand-to-action reading order; it has the same card-order and tiny-text problems.

A is the original shrunk into the centre of the banner, so it is unreadable and mostly empty. B fills the format, but the 48 Yearly card is split off below the logo on the far right, away from the 6 and 80 cards, a column of tiny legal text wedges between them, and the CTA comes before the headline and brand.
